label: Testimonials Card
title: Testimonials Card
summary: Use a Testimonials Card for one customer quote, their initials or photo, their name, and their words, usually in a sideways row.
corePrinciple: A real person, in their own words.

configuration.title: Initials or a photo, at three sizes
configuration.description: The card always shows an Avatar, and avatarProps sets it: monogram shows the person’s initials, and imageSource shows their photo. Without avatarProps it shows the initials of the title. Avatar Size on the card’s modes sets it to 42, 36, or 29 px; an Avatar Size in avatarProps’ own modes wins.
specimen: Renewing my car insurance took a minute.

states.title: A quote, or one button
states.description: Without onPress the card is text, and screen readers read it once: “Testimonial from Aarav S.: …”. With onPress the whole card is one button, so give it an accessibilityLabel that says where it goes; it dims while pressed and has no hover look. disabled dims it to half, stops presses, and takes it out of the Tab order.

sizing.title: 180 px wide, as tall as its quote
sizing.description: The card is always 180 px wide and never stretches to its host. Its height follows the quote: 12 px of padding, the 42 px avatar, 12 px, the name on a 16 px line, 2 px, then 16 px for each line of the quote. With a one-line quote it is 112 px tall, as in Figma.

content.title: Their name, their words
content.description: Write title as the person’s name the way they’d sign it, such as Aarav S., not the product. Write body as what they said, in a sentence or two. Screen readers read the name and the whole quote together, and cards in a row look best with quotes of similar length.

inContext.title: A row of quotes
inContext.description: Customer quotes scroll sideways under a section title, and each card opens that customer’s full review. The cards keep their 180 px, so the row scrolls instead of squeezing them.

sources.title: Use the public Testimonials Card contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (27 October build of Biscuit’s main) from the team’s private package repository. Figma’s card has Title and Body text properties and Show Footer Text and Show Button switches, but none of them changes a layer. The package matches Figma’s #0d0d0f for the name and the quote and its 112 px one-line card. monogram alone in avatarProps shows initials, and a pressable card dims while pressed.
